chunks: A number of our companions, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from al-Husayn ibn Sa'id, from al-Nadr ibn Suwayd, from Ayyub ibn al-Hurr and Imran ibn Ali, from Abu Basir, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said:
We are those firmly rooted in knowledge, and we know its interpretation.

key_terms.الرَّاسِخُونَ فِي الْعِلْمِ: Those firmly rooted in knowledge — a Quranic designation (3:7) claimed by the Imam as applying to the Ahl al-Bayt
key_terms.تَأْوِيل: Ta'wil — the inner, authoritative interpretation of the Quran, as opposed to the apparent (zahir) meaning

ai.seo_question: Who are 'those firmly rooted in knowledge' (al-rasikhun fi al-'ilm) according to Shia hadith?
ai.summary: Imam al-Sadiq (AS) applies the Quranic phrase 'those firmly rooted in knowledge' (al-rasikhun fi al-'ilm) from Surah Al Imran (3:7) exclusively to the Imams of the Ahl al-Bayt, asserting that they alone possess the authoritative knowledge of the Quran's inner meanings (ta'wil). In the Quranic verse, God distinguishes between those who follow the mutashabihat (ambiguous verses) seeking discord and those with deep-rooted knowledge who submit to God's wisdom. The Imam's statement to his companions declares that the Ahl al-Bayt are those deep-rooted ones, and that the ta'wil — the esoteric, authoritative interpretation — belongs to them.
